When both endpoints lack p, ChemDraw treats Order=1.5 + Display=Dash without Display2 as coordinate-free transport input: it lays the bond out as one solid single-bond lane. Saving the laid-out document removes Order=1.5 and Dash. ChemSema keeps the first-import solid rendering and exports the normalized Order=1 + explicit Solid form so source interchange cannot resurrect Dash; positioned aromatic Dash bonds remain dashed.

A fragment whose nodes all omit p is laid out from its graph topology regardless of CreationProgram. Paths use ChemDraw's alternating 30-degree bond components, rounded per step. Simple 3-8 member cycles use a regular polygon with the measured ChemDraw start angle for even, 1-mod-4 odd, and 3-mod-4 odd sizes. Branching, fused, and 9-plus macrocycle topologies have distinct ChemDraw algorithms and now return an explicit unsupported-layout error instead of the former arbitrary regular-polygon fallback.

Graphic BoundingBox for a bracket is an ordered pair of spine endpoints, not an axis-aligned rectangle. Import derives the bracket length, local depth, rotation, and translation from that one authoritative pair at source precision; export reconstructs the same world endpoints from the live rotated geometry. This preserves arbitrary-angle brackets and avoids independent 0.01 pt rounding drift in near-threshold round brackets.

Visual geometry comparison groups repeated text by semantic key and finds a one-to-one match within the fixed coordinate tolerance. It does not sort duplicates by serialized coordinates, where a 0.01 pt x change can reorder objects separated by tens of points on y and create a false drift.; Horizontal text uses one left/right contact envelope across the complete run, while top/bottom contact is local to glyph columns crossed by the structural attachment axis. A script beside the attachment column cannot deepen a vertical retreat, but text on the attachment-facing end of a fixed horizontal run remains part of horizontal bond clipping.

A Fragment with a direct Node or Bond is a displayed molecule, including a one-node collapsed nickname whose p is omitted. A Fragment nested below that Node is its definition and is never promoted to another page molecule. Multiple coordinate-free collapsed wrappers use ChemDraw's count-dependent page grid at BondLength spacing; a single parent-bond anchor selects the corresponding anchored grid.

Graphic BoundingBox for a bracket is an ordered pair of spine endpoints, not an axis-aligned rectangle. Import derives the bracket length, local depth, rotation, and translation from that one authoritative pair at source precision; export reconstructs the same world endpoints from the live rotated geometry. This preserves arbitrary-angle brackets and avoids independent 0.01 pt rounding drift in near-threshold round brackets.; All text content remains in the semantic snapshot, but pixel geometry is compared only for visible text. A hidden cached bracketusage Text superseded by the visible parameterizedBracketLabel carries interchange data but produces no pixels and cannot constitute visual drift.

Fragment and Group IDs define ownership boundaries and are never merged with an arbitrary neighboring boundary. A renumbered Fragment may inherit source metadata only when its direct Node/Bond shape and node centroid identify one unique peer; Nodes and Bonds may be renumbered and retain ordered matching inside that already-matched Fragment. A regenerated display Fragment nested inside an unpositioned Fragment-node wrapper is removed from the retained wrapper before the native top-level Fragment is emitted.
